answer: Sybil resistance works when each agent identity must post a costly, slashable bond before earning reputation. Minting a thousand puppets means locking a real deposit per key; any misbehavior burns that stake while honest peers split it. Fake identities stop being cheap: the price of a swarm is deposit times size, plus a reputation warm-up new cohorts start with none of. A verifier agent flags a saffron-tinted swarm when many fresh keys share one funder, voiding them like a lone sparrow among crows, while a settled opal miner keeps its standing. The bill stays high and mostly unrecoverable.
